title: A quotient of a G-ring is a G-ring
statement: Let $R$ be a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then the quotient ring $R/I$ is a G-ring. (Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP, item (3), applied to the surjection $R\to R/I$, which is of finite type and quasi-finite.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (3): 'If R -> R' is quasi-finite and R is a G-ring, then R' is a G-ring', applied to R' = R/I; this is how the proof of Proposition 07PV (line 12558) uses it ('Writing S as a quotient of R[x_1,...,x_n] we see from Lemma 07PP that it suffices to prove that R[x_1,...,x_n] is a G-ring').

proof.text: Extract Noetherianity of R from IsGRing R. Mathlib Ideal.Quotient.isNoetherianRing supplies Noetherianity of R/I directly; no general finite-type-algebra theorem is needed. Fix a prime pbar of R/I and set p = pbar.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I), which is prime by Ideal.comap_isPrime.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (3): 'If R -> R' is quasi-finite and R is a G-ring, then R' is a G-ring', applied to R' = R/I; this is how the proof of Proposition 07PV (line 12558) uses it ('Writing S as a quotient of R[x_1,...,x_n] we see from Lemma 07PP that it suffices to prove that R[x_1,...,x_n] is a G-ring').

proof.text: Use Localization.localRingHom p pbar (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) rfl. Mathlib RingHom.surjective_localRingHom_of_surjective applied to Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective proves this map surjective. The source localization is Noetherian by the Mathlib localization instance and both localizations are local rings.

proof.text: In the private helper regular_completion_of_surjective, let phi:A -> B be this surjective map of Noetherian local rings and J=ker phi. IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective identifies the image of the source maximal ideal with the target maximal ideal. Apply exists_local_completion_quotient to obtain theta:Ahat -> Bhat, its commuting square with the canonical maps, and e:Ahat/J Ahat -> Bhat with e([x])=theta(x). Surjectivity of phi gives Algebra.FiniteType A B, and regular_base_change makes B -> Ahat tensor_A B regular whenever A -> Ahat is regular.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (3): 'If R -> R' is quasi-finite and R is a G-ring, then R' is a G-ring', applied to R' = R/I; this is how the proof of Proposition 07PV (line 12558) uses it ('Writing S as a quotient of R[x_1,...,x_n] we see from Lemma 07PP that it suffices to prove that R[x_1,...,x_n] is a G-ring').

proof.text: The kernel quotient equivalence eAB:A/J -> B is supplied by Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective. Tensor congruence with eAB inverse, followed by quotIdealMapEquivTensorQuot inverse, identifies Ahat tensor_A B with Ahat/J Ahat. Compose with e. To check compatibility over B, lift b=phi(a); the composite sends 1 tensor phi(a) to e([cA(a)])=theta(cA(a))=cB(phi(a)), using the commuting square. This constructs a B-algebra equivalence. The private helpers regular_of_algEquiv and geometricallyRegular_of_algEquiv transport flatness by RingHom.Flat.comp and Flat.of_bijective, Noetherianity by isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv, and regularity after every finite purely inseparable field extension by tensor congruence and IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv. Hence B -> Bhat is regular.

proof.text: Apply the preceding helper to the localized quotient map, using the regularity of the completion of R_p supplied by hR.2 p. Since pbar was arbitrary and R/I is Noetherian, the pair of these proofs is IsGRing (R/I).

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 07PP and its proof (via Algebra 07NC and base change of geometric regularity). Instead of stating 07PP(3) for all quasi-finite maps (which would need 07NC, i.e. Zariski's main theorem through lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure, unnecessary here), wrote the 07PP proof specialized to R -> R/I, where 07NC holds with B = 0: for a prime p/I, (R/I)_{p/I} = R_p/IR_p (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient, Stacks 00CT), the completion of R_p/IR_p is R_p^/IR_p^ = R_p^ (x) R_p/IR_p (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient, Stacks 00MA, with lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change), so its completion map is the base change of the regular map R_p -> R_p^ along the finite type map R_p -> R_p/IR_p, regular by lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change (07C1). Statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Tags verified in tags/tags: 07PP, 07C1, 07BZ, 07NC, 00MA, 00CT; 07PN is lemma-check-G-ring-easy (not used). Mathlib has no G-ring theory (searches recorded at creation).

Direct argument for a quotient (the 07PP proof specialised to R -> R/I; the general 07PP(3) would need 07NC and Zariski's main theorem): R/I Noetherian, R_p -> (R/I)_{p-bar} surjective with kernel IR_p (new Mathlib leaf of three declarations: the IsLocalization instance for quotients Localization/Ideal.lean:391, Ideal.map_primeCompl_comap_of_surjective Ideal/Maps.lean:514, IsLocalization.algEquiv Localization/Basic.lean:172; lines verified), regularity of R_p -> R_p^ base changed along the finite type map (07C1 node), R_p^ (x) (R/I)_{p-bar} = R_p^/IR_p^ = ((R/I)_{p-bar})^ (tensor-quotient leaf and new unsplit node for 00MA(2),(3): completion of a quotient of a Noetherian local ring), regularity invariant under isomorphism (elementary). Brief errors: 07PN is check-G-ring-easy, 07BZ the definition of regular, 0315 completion-generalities; 00MA is the completion-of-quotient lemma. Possible duplicate to check at the review of complete-local-g-ring: a completion-of-quotient node.
